(4) Hermes' skill write-approval gate is opt-in (skills.write_approval default False). Only unattended replace/remove of memory is fail-closed by default. (5) The 'seeded eval proves the loop' is not reference-derived: no reference evaluates learning outcomes (the Hermes record flags this as a weakness). (6) Claude's inclusion in the proposal cluster rests on lazy module names (tool_cell_skill_proposal/suggestion) and analytics events. That is a skill-authoring proposal UI, not evidence of an approval-gated learning loop. Cursor's Bugbot learned rules are PR-review specific.
